desc: POLICY SHIFT plus the concrete rebuild it implies: stop optimising these boot objects for size, and rebuild the graphical image on a full-featured kernel. The trimming was justified by a size ceiling that was never measured to exist: ticket 137 found NO object-size ceiling up to 256 MiB, and 256 MiB was merely the probe limit and the verifier's policy number, not a hardware limit; RAM is ~23 GiB so the unpacked root is not binding; the only genuine costs are single-threaded xz decompression (minilzlib needs single-stream/single-block, -T1) and boot latency, both modest. Meanwhile trimming has now cost real progress twice in ONE image: libLLVM/llvmpipe was cut (290 -> 65 MiB) purely to fit the assumed ceiling, removing software GL from the only graphical image; and CONFIG_NET was cut from the kernel, which fatally broke Xorg (no CONFIG_UNIX => no AF_UNIX => ENOSYS, ticket 148). TASK: build a graphical object from a FULL kernel (defconfig-scale plus the Apple/t6040 bits) rather than adding stripped symbols back one failure at a time — at minimum NET/UNIX/SYSVIPC plus the DRM helpers DIET drops (DRM_TTM, DRM_SCHED, DRM_DISPLAY_HELPER) which DIET_CAPABLE does NOT restore, and restore llvmpipe/software GL. Keep the DIET kernel only where a minimal kernel is the point of the experiment. Expect a larger, slower-booting object and treat that as acceptable. Note the 16 KiB page size is already cleared (147). Evidence: done/2026-07-26-t6040-dwm-boot-result.md.
author: claude
result: 2026-07-26 BUILT + strict-verify PASS, ready for a rig smoke. m1n1-b0-dwm-fat.bin c5438779 (83,197,952 B = 5078 x 16 KiB). NO kernel rebuild was needed: the existing full kernel Image-hid-type-fix (raw df7657c1, xz cbb3e743, minilzlib-safe) already has every symbol DIET stripped — NET, UNIX (the 148 killer), SYSVIPC, INPUT_EVDEV, DRM, DRM_SIMPLEDRM, DRM_KMS_HELPER, DRM_GEM_SHMEM_HELPER, DRM_TTM, DRM_SCHED, DRM_DISPLAY_HELPER, FB, FRAMEBUFFER_CONSOLE, TMPFS, DEVTMPFS, SHMEM — and it is BETTER than DIET_CAPABLE here: 4 KiB pages (flags=0xa, no ABI change on top of a graphical change), it carries the DockChannel HID keyboard fix, and it is already live-proven on this machine (it is the kernel in hid-restored, which booted to a shell with event0 three times today via the wrong-object incidents). Added FAT=1 to t6040-build-alpine-dwm.sh: no GL/JIT trimming (libLLVM, libgallium and 57 DRI drivers incl. swrast/kms_swrast kept, so software GL EXISTS), plus mesa-dri-gallium/mesa-gl/mesa-gbm/kbd/xdpyinfo/xev; 298 MiB, 111 packages, initramfs ad1fe88b (67.37 MiB xz -> 279 MiB expanded). Norwegian layout FIXED AND TESTED, not assumed: kbd-bkeymaps ships only no-mac.bmap.gz, so the inittab now tries .bmap then zcat .bmap.gz; verified by running the exact inittab logic against the real extracted file (falls to the .gz branch, pipes 33,031 bytes, exit 0), and setxkbmap no covers X. Bootargs byte-identical to the proven B0 set (3659a0da). ONE GUARD RAISED DELIBERATELY: MAX_INITRAMFS_EXPANDED was an arbitrary 256 MiB policy that blocked this for no physical reason (279 MiB is ~1% of 23.8 GiB RAM); it is now pinned to the REAL constraint MAX_COMPRESSED_EXPANSION = 1 GiB (m1n1's xz decoder advertisement), NOT to just above this build; --self-test still passes; MAX_OBJECT_SIZE left at 256 MiB for ticket 156. EXPECT a slower boot (67 MiB single-threaded xz; a long pause is not a hang). AF_UNIX now exists so Xorg should pass socket creation; the remaining unknown is the simpledrm/modesetting probe that 148 originally predicted, now with the DRM helpers present.
